Workday disclosure reference

Call Q&A coverage is incomplete; specific gaps are listed on the Sources page. Three-year histories appear where comparable disclosures exist.

Open the interactive charts · Download data · Source coverage and gaps

How to read growth

Long-term growth is the three-year compound annual growth rate (CAGR), measured between the same fiscal quarter or annual period where both endpoints exist. A two-year CAGR is labeled explicitly when a three-year endpoint is unavailable. No annualized rate is shown for shorter history. Quarter, annual, year-to-date, trailing-twelve-month and point-in-time observations remain separate.

Latest growth compares each observation with the same period one year earlier: (current ÷ prior − 1) × 100. Acceleration is latest year-on-year growth minus the year-on-year rate one year earlier, in percentage points. This compares two annual growth rates; it is not sequential-quarter growth. Percentage metrics use percentage-point changes, and their long-term column shows annualized percentage-point change. Percent growth is not shown from a zero or negative base, or to a negative endpoint. Targets, irregular event periods and open-ended thresholds do not receive exact growth rates.

Teal means the growth rate increased; magenta means it decreased. Neither color is an investment recommendation. Higher expenses, taxes, dilution or debt can be unfavorable. Dots are actual disclosed observations; gaps are not interpolated. Dollar amounts are displayed in millions where the source data are in dollars. Every value retains its own source link.

Period and accounting conventions

Workday’s fiscal year ends January 31. Q2 FY2027 ended July 31, 2026. The main window is July 2023 through July 2026, with FY2023 and early-2023 comparison anchors retained where available. Latest available filing presentations are used, which can restate or round older values. Additive cash-flow and income-statement quarters may be derived from annual/YTD differences; the source notes identify these. EPS, margins and weighted-average shares are not calculated by subtracting annual amounts. GAAP and non-GAAP are separate series. Acquisition-specific and other dimensional footnote facts are not combined with consolidated totals. Disclosure tags that change are not silently joined.

Cash & investments

Accretion (Amortization) of Discounts and Premiums, Investments

The sum of the periodic adjustments of the differences between securities' face values and purchase prices that are charged against earnings. This is called accretion if the security was purchased at a discount and amortization if it was purchased at premium. As a noncash item, this element is an adjustment to net income when calculating cash provided by or used in operations using the indirect method.

Additional Paid in Capital

Excess of issue price over par or stated value of the entity's capital stock and amounts received from other transactions involving the entity's stock or stockholders. Includes adjustments to additional paid in capital. Some examples of such adjustments include recording the issuance of debt with a beneficial conversion feature and certain tax consequences of equity instruments awarded to employees. Use this element for the aggregate amount of additional paid-in capital associated with common and preferred stock. For additional paid-in capital associated with only common stock, use the element additional paid in capital, common stock. For additional paid-in capital associated with only preferred stock, use the element additional paid in capital, preferred stock.

Number of Operating Segments

An operating segment is a component of an enterprise: (a) that engages in business activities from which it may earn revenues and incur expenses (including revenues and expenses relating to transactions with other components of the same enterprise), (b) whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the enterprise's chief operating decision maker to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segment and assess its performance, and (c) for which discrete financial information is available. An operating segment may engage in business activities for which it has yet to earn revenues, for example, start-up operations may be operating segments before earning revenues.

The aggregate expense charged against earnings to allocate the cost of intangible assets (nonphysical assets not used in production) in a systematic and rational manner to the periods expected to benefit from such assets. Share-based Compensation Arrangement by Share-based Payment Award, Fair Value Assumptions, Expected Volatility Rate, Maximum — Employee Stock

The estimated measure of the maximum percentage by which a share price is expected to fluctuate during a period. Volatility also may be defined as a probability-weighted measure of the dispersion of returns about the mean. The volatility of a share price is the standard deviation of the continuously compounded rates of return on the share over a specified period. That is the same as the standard deviation of the differences in the natural logarithms of the stock prices plus dividends, if any, over the period.

Taxes

Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (Loss), Net of Tax

Accumulated change in equity from transactions and other events and circumstances from non-owner sources, net of tax effect, at period end. Excludes Net Income (Loss), and accumulated changes in equity from transactions resulting from investments by owners and distributions to owners. Includes foreign currency translation items, certain pension adjustments, unrealized gains and losses on certain investments in debt and equity securities, other than temporary impairment (OTTI) losses related to factors other than credit losses on available-for-sale and held-to-maturity debt securities that an entity does not intend to sell and it is not more likely than not that the entity will be required to sell before recovery of the amortized cost basis, as well as changes in the fair value of derivatives related to the effective portion of a designated cash flow hedge.
